title: Cart lab: change driving force
target: Use controlled data to describe how net force affects acceleration.
criteria: Change driving force while keeping total mass fixed.
Use data or a graph to compare accelerations.
Explain how resistance affects the ideal relationship.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: How can a cart-and-hanger setup increase driving force while keeping total moving mass fixed?
options: Transfer a small mass from the cart to the hanger.
Add new mass to the hanger from outside the system.
Keep the hanging mass fixed and add mass only to the cart.
cpa.guide: Redistributing existing mass increases hanger weight without changing total moving mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Adding a mass from a supply box to the hanger changes which two quantities?
options: Hanger weight and total moving mass.
cpa.guide: The added object contributes both gravitational driving force and inertia.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg system experiences net forces of 8 N and 20 N in two trials. What accelerations are predicted?
cpa.guide: Divide each net force by the fixed 4 kg mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: At fixed mass, net force rises by a factor of 1.5. How should acceleration change?
cpa.guide: a = F_net/m is linear in net force for fixed mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A drive force is 14 N while resistance is 2 N opposite motion. Which force enters a = F_net/m?
cpa.guide: Subtract opposing resistance to obtain net force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A graph of acceleration against applied pull does not pass through the origin. What might explain this?
options: An automatic change in units from m/s² to kg.
An opposing resistive force that was not subtracted from the applied pull.
A requirement that all experimental data be erased.
A proof that net force never affects acceleration.
cpa.guide: Applied pull can differ from net force; resistance shifts the relationship.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
